title: Isaiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Isaiah 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The burden of the valley of vision.
Thou that art full of stirs, a tumultuous city.
All thy rulers are fled together.
For it is a day of trouble.
questions.correctAnswer: The burden of the valley of vision.
questions.explanation: This is the first statement in the chapter, found in Isaiah 22:1.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 22:2 say about the slain men?
options: They are slain with the sword.
Thy slain men are not slain with the sword.
questions.correctAnswer: Thy slain men are not slain with the sword.
questions.explanation: This is a direct quote from Isaiah 22:2.

questions.question: What is happening to the rulers in Isaiah 22:3?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Isaiah 22:3, where it mentions all rulers have fled.

questions.question: What does the speaker do in Isaiah 22:4?
questions.explanation: This action is described in Isaiah 22:4, where the speaker expresses sorrow.

questions.question: What is described in Isaiah 22:5?
options: A day of trouble and perplexity.
questions.correctAnswer: A day of trouble and perplexity.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:5 clearly states it is a day of trouble.

questions.question: What does Elam bear according to Isaiah 22:6?
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Isaiah 22:6, where Elam is described bearing a quiver with chariots.

questions.question: What shall happen to the choicest valleys according to Isaiah 22:7?
options: They shall be filled with water.
They shall be full of chariots.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be full of chariots.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:7 states that the choicest valleys will be full of chariots.

questions.question: What did the people look to in Isaiah 22:8?
options: The armor of the house of the forest.
questions.correctAnswer: The armor of the house of the forest.
questions.explanation: This is directly mentioned in Isaiah 22:8, where they looked to the armor.

questions.question: What did the people see in Isaiah 22:9?
options: The breaches of the city of David.
questions.correctAnswer: The breaches of the city of David.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:9 states that they have seen the breaches of the city of David.

questions.question: In Isaiah 22:5, what is the Lord GOD of hosts doing?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:5 indicates that the Lord is breaking down the walls.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 22:3, how are the rulers described?
options: They are bound by the archers.
questions.correctAnswer: They are bound by the archers.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Isaiah 22:3, where rulers are described as bound.

questions.question: True or False: The valley of vision is mentioned in Isaiah 22.
questions.explanation: The valley of vision is indeed mentioned in Isaiah 22:1.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah weeps for the joy of his people in Isaiah 22.
questions.explanation: Isaiah expresses deep sorrow in Isaiah 22:4, indicating weeping for his people.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that all rulers are victorious in battle.
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the rulers have fled, not that they are victorious, as seen in Isaiah 22:3.

questions.question: True or False: Elam is described as bearing a shield in Isaiah 22.
questions.explanation: Elam is noted for bearing a quiver with chariots, not a shield, according to Isaiah 22:6.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the houses of Jerusalem according to Isaiah 22:10?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Isaiah 22:10 states that the houses have been broken down to fortify the wall.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 22:11 promise will happen if someone does not look unto the maker of the water?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Isaiah 22:11 indicates that despite efforts, they have not respected the maker, suggesting consequences for ignoring Him.

questions.question: What does the Lord call for in Isaiah 22:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:12 reveals that the Lord calls for weeping, mourning, baldness, and sackcloth.

questions.question: What is the mood of the people described in Isaiah 22:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:13 depicts the people as celebrating with joy and gluttony, saying 'let us eat and drink; for tomorrow we shall die.'

questions.question: What will happen to the iniquity mentioned in Isaiah 22:14?
options: It will not be purged until death.
questions.correctAnswer: It will not be purged until death.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:14 indicates that this iniquity shall not be purged until they die, showing the seriousness of their actions.

questions.question: Who is Shebna in Isaiah 22:15?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:15 identifies Shebna as the treasurer who is over the house, indicating his important role.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 22:16 question about Shebna's actions?
options: Why he is building a temple.
Why he is hewing out a sepulchre.
Why he is leading the people.
questions.correctAnswer: Why he is hewing out a sepulchre.
questions.explanation: The verse questions why Shebna has hewed out a sepulchre for himself, suggesting vanity and pride.

questions.question: What will happen to Shebna according to Isaiah 22:17?
options: He will be taken into captivity.
questions.correctAnswer: He will be taken into captivity.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:17 states that the Lord will carry Shebna away with a mighty captivity, signifying judgment.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 22:18, what will happen to Shebna in a large country?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:18 indicates that there Shebna shall die, showing the finality of his judgment.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 22:5 describe the day being faced?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:5 describes it as a day of trouble, treading down, and perplexity by the Lord.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 22:8 say the people looked to on that day?
options: The armor of the house of the forest.
The waters of the lower pool.
questions.correctAnswer: The armor of the house of the forest.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:8 indicates that they looked to the armor of the house of the forest, seeking strength in their own means.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 22:9 indicate about the breaches of the city of David?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:9 states that the breaches of the city of David are many, indicating a significant state of decay.

questions.question: Is it true that the people were called to mourning in Isaiah 22:12?
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Isaiah 22:12 clearly states that the Lord called to weeping and mourning.

questions.question: Is it true that the people in Isaiah 22:13 chose to mourn instead of feast?
questions.explanation: This statement is false as Isaiah 22:13 shows the people celebrating with joy, choosing to feast.

questions.question: Is it true that Shebna is commended for his actions in Isaiah 22:16?
questions.explanation: This statement is false because Isaiah 22:16 questions Shebna's actions, indicating disapproval instead of commendation.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 22.

questions.question: What will happen to Shebna according to Isaiah 22:19?
options: He will be driven from his station
He will build a new home
questions.correctAnswer: He will be driven from his station
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Isaiah 22:19 states, 'And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.'

questions.question: Who will God call to serve in place of Shebna according to Isaiah 22:20?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Isaiah 22:20 states, 'And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah.'

questions.question: What will Eliakim be a father to according to Isaiah 22:21?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:21 mentions that Eliakim 'shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 22:22, what will be placed upon Eliakim's shoulder?
options: The key of the house of David
questions.correctAnswer: The key of the house of David
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:22 states that 'the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder.'

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Isaiah 22:23 to describe Eliakim's importance?
options: A nail in a sure place
questions.correctAnswer: A nail in a sure place
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:23 uses the metaphor 'I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place' to signify Eliakim's stability and importance.

questions.question: What will happen to the nail fastened in a sure place according to Isaiah 22:25?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:25 states, 'In that day... shall the nail that is fastened in the sure place be removed, and be cut down.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'key' in Isaiah 22:22 mean?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 22:22, the Hebrew word for 'key' signifies authority, representing Eliakim's power to open and shut.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Isaiah 22:22 regarding Eliakim's authority?
questions.explanation: The phrase about the 'key' represents a metaphor for authority and control in Isaiah 22:22.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of authority in Isaiah 22:21?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:19 echoes the theme of authority, where Jesus gives Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, paralleling Eliakim's authority in Isaiah 22:21.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament reflects the concept of being a 'father' as stated in Isaiah 22:21?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 4:15 reflects the concept of spiritual fatherhood, similar to Eliakim being a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem in Isaiah 22:21.

questions.question: What comes before Isaiah 22:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:19 follows the prophecy concerning Shebna's downfall, as indicated in verses 15-18.

questions.question: Which chapter in Isaiah contains a similar theme of divine judgment as seen in Isaiah 22?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 24 discusses divine judgment, connecting to the themes of judgment and consequences in Isaiah 22.

questions.question: The key given to Eliakim signifies what aspect of leadership?
questions.explanation: The key signifies spiritual authority as Eliakim is entrusted with significant leadership, indicating God's sovereignty.

questions.question: True or False: The nail fastened in a sure place is a permanent fixture according to Isaiah 22:25.
questions.explanation: This statement is False because Isaiah 22:25 indicates that the nail will be removed and cut down.

questions.question: True or False: Eliakim's role is compared to that of a father in Isaiah 22:21.
questions.explanation: This statement is True as Isaiah 22:21 states that Eliakim 'shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.'

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 22:14 teach about human sin?
options: Iniquity remains until death without divine pardon
Sin can be fully purged by human effort
All sins are forgiven immediately upon repentance
Iniquity is irrelevant to God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Iniquity remains until death without divine pardon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:14 states, 'Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die,' teaching that certain sins remain until death without God's cleansing.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 22:22 teach about divine authority in governance?
options: God grants sovereign authority that cannot be revoked by humans
Human rulers hold ultimate power over divine decree
Authority is shared equally between God and people
Divine authority is symbolic and not operative in governance
questions.correctAnswer: God grants sovereign authority that cannot be revoked by humans
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:22 says the key of the house of David will be laid upon Eliakim's shoulder so he shall open and none shall shut, and shut and none shall open, showing God's sovereign authority in governance.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's judgment is taught in Isaiah 22:17?
options: God executes mighty captivity as punishment for sin
God ignores the sins of His people
Judgment is always delayed and uncertain
God's punishment is symbolic and not actual
questions.correctAnswer: God executes mighty captivity as punishment for sin
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:17 declares, 'the LORD will carry thee away with a mighty captivity,' illustrating God's active judgment and punishment for sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 22:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:5 describes the Lord GOD of hosts bringing trouble, treading down, and perplexity, demonstrating His sovereign control over events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 22:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:14 reveals that iniquity shall not be purged until death, demonstrating God's justice in dealing with sin.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 22:20-23 connect to the theme of messianic kingship elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the authority and office of Christ as the ultimate ruler
It denies any future kingship and focuses on prophetic ministry only
It emphasizes human kingship independent of God's will
It predicts the permanent fall of David's house without restoration
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the authority and office of Christ as the ultimate ruler
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:20-23 describes Eliakim being given the key of the house of David and authority, which typologically points forward to Christ's sovereign kingship (cf. Revelation 3:7).

questions.question: How does Isaiah 22:13 prepare for the biblical teaching on human despair and false security?
options: It illustrates the folly of hedonistic denial in the face of judgment
It encourages joyful celebration as preparation for death
It teaches that death ends all accountability
It promotes indifference toward divine warnings
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the folly of hedonistic denial in the face of judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:13 shows people indulging in eating and drinking saying 'to morrow we shall die,' revealing false security and despair without repentance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Isaiah 22:19 and Isaiah 22:21 teach about divine appointment and removal of leaders?
options: God sovereignly removes unfaithful leaders and appoints faithful ones
Human leaders choose their successors by inheritance
Leadership is permanent and unchangeable once granted
Divine will does not affect political leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly removes unfaithful leaders and appoints faithful ones
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:19 declares removal from office, while 22:21 shows God appointing Eliakim, demonstrating divine sovereignty in leadership transitions.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 22:11 and Isaiah 22:12 teach about human reliance and divine judgment?
options: Ignoring God the Maker leads to judgment and calls for repentance
Human ingenuity guarantees safety from divine judgment
Divine judgment is unrelated to human actions
Constructing defenses is praised as godly trust
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God the Maker leads to judgment and calls for repentance
questions.explanation: Verse 11 condemns lack of regard for God the Maker, while verse 12 shows God calling for mourning, indicating judgment due to human negligence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 22:16 and Isaiah 22:18 teach about pride and divine humiliation?
options: Self-exalting pride leads to violent divine humiliation and disgrace
Pride is a virtue rewarded by God
Divine judgment is mild and symbolic only
Humiliation is caused solely by human enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Self-exalting pride leads to violent divine humiliation and disgrace
questions.explanation: Verse 16 criticizes Shebna's self-carved tomb, a symbol of pride, and verse 18 foretells violent exile and shame, teaching divine response to pride.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Isaiah 22:13-14 promotes nihilism and despair. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It condemns despairing indulgence as sinful and declares iniquity remains until death
It encourages reckless living without fear of consequences
It removes all divine judgment from human life
It promotes atheism by denying God's justice
questions.correctAnswer: It condemns despairing indulgence as sinful and declares iniquity remains until death
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:13-14 critiques the 'eat and drink for tomorrow we die' mentality and pronounces that sin will not be purged until death, showing divine judgment, not nihilism.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 22:25 teach about the impermanence of divine appointments?
options: Even divinely appointed leaders can be removed by God's sovereign will
Divine appointments are eternal and unchangeable
Human authority is independent of God's will
Leaders are permanent fixtures regardless of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Even divinely appointed leaders can be removed by God's sovereign will
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:25 states the nail fastened in the sure place will be removed and fall, indicating that God can revoke leadership authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 22:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 22:12 shows God calling for weeping and mourning, indicating patient warning and opportunities to repent before judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 22:3 and Isaiah 22:4 teach about human failure and divine sorrow?
options: Human leaders' flight causes divine sorrow and lamentation
Human success is independent of God’s emotions
Divine sorrow is unrelated to human conduct
questions.correctAnswer: Human leaders' flight causes divine sorrow and lamentation
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes rulers fleeing and being bound, and verse 4 records the prophet’s bitter weeping, reflecting divine sorrow over human failure.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 22:9-10 contribute to the theological understanding of misplaced trust?
options: Trusting in human fortifications without God’s help is futile
God’s protection depends on human strength alone
Water management replaces faith in God
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in human fortifications without God’s help is futile
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 describe breaches and fortifications made by humans, yet verse 11 condemns ignoring the Maker, indicating misplaced trust in human efforts.
